items.text: A name is fixed unless it is defined with Changeable. A name of kind guarded, atomic or counter is fixed and can still be changed with Set or Add.
The kind of a name is fixed by its first definition and never changes.

A name is defined once in the block where it lives. A second definition of a name that is already visible, in the same block or an outer one, is an error. Blocks that do not contain each other may use the same name.
Names are not case-sensitive. Two names that differ only in case are an error.
A plural is a different name from its singular.
When a sentence uses a name, the longest defined name wins. Two different names of the same length are an error.
A hard word can never be part of a name.
The words the, a and an are removed from code, except A and An at the start of a sentence, which are declaration words. They are kept in raw text and printed text.
Say prints a value when the whole line is one value. Otherwise the line is text, and each word equal to a defined name is replaced by its value. literally prints the word.
Sentences run from top to bottom. A function, record, enum or interface may be used above its definition. Every other name must be defined above its first use.
Inside one sentence, operands are read from left to right.
A sentence holds one operation.
A number without a point is a whole number. A number with a point is a decimal.
A whole number and a decimal in one operation is an error.
A conversion between kinds is always written with as.
divided by gives a decimal. whole divided by gives a whole number, moving toward zero.
Rounding goes half away from zero unless rounded to even is written.
Whole-number overflow stops the program in every build.
Whole division by zero stops the program.
Decimals follow IEEE rules, with infinity, minus infinity and not a number.
Lists and text positions count from 1.
item N of list out of range stops the program. safe item gives a maybe value.
Maps and sets keep insertion order. A key that is not in a map gives missing.
Text compares case-sensitively, by Unicode code point.
Two lists are equal when they have the same items in the same order.
Sorting goes smallest first. descending reverses it.
A maybe value must be checked or given a fallback before use.
A can fail operation must be handled with Try or a default.
A bug stops the program: drops run, a plain trace prints, and the exit code is 1.

A Look at must cover every shape of the enum.
Every value has exactly one owner.
give moves a value, and the old name is dead.
Inputs are lent for reading by default.
A value has many shared borrows or one unique borrow, never both.
A borrow ends at its last use.
Records, lists, maps and enums own their parts and cannot hold a borrow.
A function gives back owned values only.
A temporary value lives to the end of its sentence.
Values are freed in reverse order of definition.
copy of makes a deep copy.
A share value is immutable. Changing it needs guarded.
A cycle of shared values leaks memory and never corrupts it.
A value that crosses tasks is given, shared and immutable, guarded or atomic.
Tasks started in a Do these together. block all end before the block ends.
Cancellation is cooperative, and the block ends with the first failure.
A guarded value is never held across Wait for.
Sending on a closed channel fails. Receiving from a closed empty channel gives missing.
Modules start once, in order of dependency, before the program body. A cycle is an error.
